errors: No error in the theory: the vector identity, (III) and (IV), and the position-angle conversions (ζ+ν, ζ+ν−p, ζ+ν+M) all check.
Transferring great-circle directions from the star to the Moon's centre is an explicit small-angle approximation, justified only by the small separation (~16'). Gauss flags it ('ohne Bedenken').

Trial 1: log θ must be 3.49900n (giving −3155.0s = −52m35.0s, the value used). The written '3.54581n' / '−3518.0' (as transcribed) does not match the preceding logarithms; this is either a misreading or a slip that did not propagate.
Trial 2: from log cosν = 9.74451n I get ν ≈ 123°44'30". The written value appears to be 123°43'47", a discrepancy of under 1'.

Trial 2: the position angle 'Ost v. Aeq. 156°28'' implies ν ≈ 146°17', inconsistent with ν ≈ 123°44' of the same column, which would give ζ+ν ≈ 133°55'. The derived 147°13' and 128°53' are internally consistent with 156°28'. Either a slip by Gauss or a value carried from another computation; unresolved.
Altitude uses the unreduced log P = 3.55854 (sea-level parallax) rather than 3.55765; a harmless convention.
The previous-page transcription b = P cos z cos M should be P sin z cos M; the page's own computation of altitude uses sin z.

results.what: Occultation/contact theory by orthographic projection on the plane through the Earth's centre perpendicular to the star: path parameters (ζ, n, η, Θ), observer coordinates a = P cosφ sinh, b = P sinφ cosδ − P cosφ sinδ cosh, contact condition cosν = q sin(ζ−μ)/ϱ, θ = q cos(ζ−μ+ν)/(n cosν), with the sign of sinν choosing immersion or emersion.
results.modern_name: Fundamental-plane (Besselian-type) method for occultations and eclipses
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1778–82) for analytic projection treatments; F. W. Bessel (1820s occultation method; 'Analyse der Finsternisse', 1842) for the standard form

results.what: Position angle of contact from the south limb point relative to the equator, ecliptic and vertical: ζ+ν, ζ+ν−p, ζ+ν+M, with M the parallactic-type angle from tan M = a/b.
results.modern_name: Position angle / vertex angle of contact in occultation predictions

results.what: Determining the longitude (or the contact times) by trying hour angles and interpolating until the implied longitude equals the known value (30m23s).
results.modern_name: Iterative / regula falsi solution for longitude from occultations

deep.surprise_reason: Projecting onto a plane perpendicular to the star with Besselian-like path elements predates Bessel's published occultation theory if this dates from c.1809. However, analytic projection methods (Lagrange and others) already existed, and Gauss's interest in eclipse and occultation reductions is known. This is a careful, competent working example rather than a new result.
